raw_evidence: Inhale Me, Exhale You By Kate Partington Tue 2 Jun 10:00 - Mon 28 Sep 22:00 Art Tue 2 Jun - Mon 28 Sep From 10:00 Tue 2 Jun - Mon 28 Sep From 10:00 Arches Windows No booking required Unspoken feelings and moments of desire You can see this artwork in HOME Arches Windows on Whitwo This piece belongs to a wider series called ‘Desire Me.’ It aims to translate unspoken feelings and moments of desire that occur between us The focus is on longing, on reaching out and on instances of hopeful touch that happen in the early stages of a relationship. It seeks to capture the essence of sensations you get in your stomach that are so hard to verbalise, but that we all know and feel.” Kate Partington’s practice explores the subtleties of touch, connection, and the spaces that exist between bodies She is a mixed media artist working across analogue and digital spaces, constructing images that hover between materiality and emotion Her work examines how intimacy can be both tender and elusive, how connection can be felt rather than seen

Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. The Grade II-listed structure was a gift from Beijing to the people of Manchester, assembled by Chinese artisans between 1986-87 Works will begin on a two-year project of repair and restoration on Sat 12 Sep. In recent years, some elements have degraded, posing a risk to the arch itself and to the safety of the public who pass beneath To carry out repairs, materials and artisans from China will be sourced so that every facet of its restoration remains true to the culture which it honours. This is part of a wider regeneration of the Chinatown area as the Council works to invest more into the amenity and upkeep Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin, Executive Member for Clean Air, Environment and Transport, said: “For generations this arch has been a focal point for the Chinese community in Manchester. raw_evidence: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. This awareness is called common knowledge – and it has a momentous impact on our social, political, and economic lives Common knowledge can make sense of financial bubbles and crashes, revolutions that come out of nowhere, the posturing and pretence of diplomacy, the eruption of social media shaming mobs and academic cancel culture, and the awkwardness of a first date But people also go to great lengths to avoid common knowledge―to ensure that even if everyone knows something, they can’t know that everyone else knows they know it. raw_evidence: A unique classical concert which aims to improve the experience of people with hearing loss who want to enjoy music is coming to Manchester this October Academics from the Cadenza Project, working with the Manchester Camerata orchestra, are inviting people with and without hearing loss to a special research show at the Stoller Hall on Thu 29 Oct. The concert will feature Beethoven’s Symphony No. 6, the Pastoral Symphony The Cadenza project, led by the University of Salford, is researching how to improve music for people with hearing loss. The free concert is a unique opportunity to shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying live music Trevor Cox, Professor of acoustic engineering at the University of Salford, explains: “We don’t think anything like this has been attempted before. When people suffer hearing loss, the main treatment is a hearing aid. But the devices are designed for speech. Music is an afterthou “But music is such an important part of our lives, it brings us together for shared experiences that people with hearing issues can feel locked out of. Live classical music is particularly hard for hearing aids to deal with, as it ranges from extremely quiet to very louder, over “This is a unique opportunity for people, both with hearing problems and those who hear normally, to help shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying the fabulous Camerata.”

Having ended her marriage the year she turned 40 and begun questioning the life she once imagined for hersel A former features editor at a glossy fashion magazine, she finds work at a local newspaper – and is promptly tasked with interviewing a series of distressingly inspiring women who appear to be effortlessly balancing successful careers with motherhood. Initially, these encounters Inspired by Kerr’s own experiences, Spent Hen gradually moves from isolation towards tentative optimism, as its protagonist begins speaking openly about miscarriage, infertility and childlessness, finding that the stories she has kept to herself resonate far more widely than she As Kerr questions the images of perfect families that can alienate those who cannot or do not have children, the play grows into a candid, wry exploration of grief and identity, while thoughtfully confronting the social pressure to conform to a rigid conception of a fulfilled lif Spent Hen runs at 53two from Wed 21 to Fri 23 October, before heading to Audenshaw’s Guide Bridge Theatre on Wed 28 Oct
